payload.entry: PLANNING EVIDENCE: No prior phase work notes; clean base 078e3da1d6. Existing import-budget tests pass 5/5 at 2860 first-party modules against strict 2861, but historical d3d26a5b55 reproduces the exact 2863-vs-2861 AssertionError. Same-interpreter split replays: eef22a0124 adds 3 modules and bffbc8effd adds 5. Prototype normalized source-token bytes across changed source files grow only 288 and 59 respectively (prompt staging split 362fcb2e7f: 69). Authored and validated a medium tale replacing tight module counting with a shared normalized-source-footprint guard while retaining deferred modules, CPU, and loose total limits. No implementation changes made; phase remains in progress for the plan handoff. No epic-symbol entries found.

INVESTIGATION: At sase 078e3da1d6, the three October 30 examples do not show stale rows newly reaching master after close. Cleanup 0060c20fd7 (09:10:20Z) precedes sase-1pj.4.1 close (09:15:20Z); f7eb80c7a8 (09:48:21Z) precedes sase-1pj.5.1.3 close (09:53:33Z); 7da649b562 (16:19:49Z) precedes sase-1pj.5.1.4 close (16:57:24Z). The .4 history explicitly records an upstream-row close refusal before cleanup publication. ToolRun 3ca0ba01382eb58f81f4b5063766ebe1 started at 16:59:15Z for 16a--1 from older HEAD db37d68096 (14:14:05Z), with Justfile untouched. That HEAD is an ancestor of 7da649b562 and retains all eight obsolete rows. This proves a stale observer checkout against live closed-bead status, not a broken contemporary master. The approved parent scope remains sase-o7 only. Prepared a medium tale for an early evidence-based stale-checkout verification refusal and regression coverage, preserving the existing close guard and Symvision policy. No production code changed; implementation and phase closure remain for the plan coder.

PLANNING EVIDENCE: Clean base 078e3da1d6a784cfc8fd2ab783273246318660c2, zsh 5.9; no prior phase work notes or landed fix to test_zsh_smoke.py (last change 82fae375ba, 2026-09-15). The unchanged helper uses inherited PATH when bin_dir is omitted. A logged fixture shows sbd sh calls no backend, but sbd show --for invokes <completion><candidates><bead> before inserting --format. Immediate empty fixture response: startup 0.343s, completion 0.281s, exact expected buffer. Delaying only that response 6s: startup 0.339s, completion timeout 5.025s, exact reported symptom (only b'sbd show --for' received). Controlled delay reproduction, not a fresh natural full-lane reproduction. Existing ZDOTDIR and zsh disk cache are per invocation. One medium tale is sufficient: default test-owned candidate executable, inherited-PATH sentinel regression, unchanged real-zsh assertions/timeouts, bounded loaded module runs and check. Plan sase_plan_zsh_completion_pty_isolation.md validated with zero warnings; submitting it before source changes. No tracked files changed. No epic-symbol entries currently. Implementation and closure belong to the approved coder; this is planning evidence, not a TASK RESOLVED claim.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-1gz root cause was FederationLock lifetime — PreparedListener held the flock File handle by value so a cloned descriptor (try_clone / dup) kept the flock alive after drop, turning the next symlink-rejection path into AlreadyRunning instead of UnsafeSocket. Base sase-core 16a3ed0f. Fix: crates/sase_gateway/src/federation_worker/imp/listener.rs wraps the lock File in FederationLock guard with explicit fs2 unlock on Drop, so drop always releases even with duplicates alive; plus 6 listener_lock_tests. Evidence: baseline reproduced natural flake (ipc test failed iter 9/20 and 10/30 with AlreadyRunning); new deterministic test duplicate_descriptor_does_not_block_symlink_rejection failed pre-fix (got AlreadyRunning) and passes post-fix; 6 focused tests pass 100/100; loaded loop 20/20 gateway-lib passes (249 tests); mutation checks (0600->0644 fails mode assert, symlink bypass changes UnsafeSocket to Bind) restored; full sase-core check ToolRun f0bef2d0e68520ec96d40a4dbf7f2626 green; cargo fmt -p sase_gateway --check clean; git diff is only listener.rs.

Verified: sase-core check ToolRun f0bef2d0e68520ec96d40a4dbf7f2626 green (exit 0); 6 listener_lock_tests 100/100; loaded 20/20 gateway-lib (249 tests); fmt clean; diff only listener.rs. Parent epic and seed task left for lander.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-13a — zsh PTY smoke helper no longer forks an inherited live `sase` when `bin_dir` is omitted.

Base: 078e3da1d6a784cfc8fd2ab783273246318660c2, zsh 5.9. Last test_zsh_smoke.py change remained 82fae375ba (2026-09-15). Natural flake was not observed on the unchanged module (ToolRun 2d80d9ef83ea69fe2c0923e55c875282: 4/4 workers, 21 passed in 9.26s). Controlled delayed-reply reproduction retained as evidence.

Before (logged empty fixture, existing `_read_until` budgets unchanged):
- `sbd sh`: no candidate call; startup 0.349s; completion 0.272s; buffer `sbd show `
- `sbd show --for` immediate: log `<completion><candidates><bead>`; startup 0.350s; completion 0.265s; buffer `sbd show --format `
- `sbd show --for` with 6s fixture delay: same log; startup 0.353s; completion timeout 5.025s; received only `sbd show --for`

Fix: `_pty_capture_completion` always prepends a test-owned `sase` to PATH. Explicit `bin_dir` is unchanged. Omitted `bin_dir` gets a per-capture logged empty-candidate fixture under `pty-sase-<nonce>/`. Live compsys, alias expansion, TAB, capture-widget, and timeout budgets are unchanged.

Sentinel regression `test_pty_capture_without_bin_dir_ignores_inherited_sase`:
- Original helper: ToolRun 4f4a3548f404a3372f3077f00fafa79b FAILED; exact buffer still `sbd show --format `, inherited sentinel was invoked (`assert not sentinel_log.exists()`).
- After fix: ToolRun ed8234978402aa4fdac6cc9f63aa7909; sentinel + both static alias parameters 3 passed.

After inherited 6s slow-provider probe (no `bin_dir`): startup 0.411s; completion 0.328s (inside 5s budget); buffer `sbd show --format `; inherited sentinel never invoked.

Loaded module runs (SASE_PYTEST_WORKERS=4, distinct TMPDIR, 22 tests including sentinel):
- 3a8e7de191f6562d30018c586a6339c3: 4/4 workers, 22 passed in 9.91s
- 551d056cb37f380233c206261e57f148: 4/4 workers, 22 passed in 9.67s
- 07db0f3bd2a2b7f406a2b4d379dde92c: 4/4 workers, 22 passed in 8.76s

`sase tool run check` b6a56cfa45850e3172adeb78a4f3323e succeeded (triage pass/exited_zero). test (scoped) 38m 47s exit 0; selector escalated to the full suite (`core-identity-changed`). No skips, xfails, timeout raises, or flake-baseline edits.

Limits: injected 6s delay is a controlled subprocess stall, not a fresh natural full-lane reproduction. Dynamic callers still supply their own fixtures and call-count/log assertions. Leave sase-13a and epic sase-1qn to the lander. No --epic-symbol entries for this phase.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-19m — _wait_for_usage now drains stderr already in the pipe before and after kill, so rate-limit text written before the deadline classifies as rate_limited; timeout without that evidence stays timeout. The isolate wrapper keeps a completed worker observation when the outer deadline races the last stdout read. test_agy_usage_probe_timeout_with_rate_limit_stderr_is_rate_limited uses a ready-file sync (expired deadline after stderr flush) plus collect classification; 20/20 serial, 55 xdist probe tests, node 0.12s.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: scoped check ToolRun 4062c1f3bb6b5a9d84097982381aef9f failed unrelated parallel-lane nodes. bead_claim_checks empty holders / missing tombstone matches sase-1oo; dismiss leftover keys matches sase-1pr; group revive extra agents matches sase-1on. Those nodes passed serially on this tree.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: test_pending_actions.py::test_transport_adapter_preserves_handled_state_and_original_lifecycle KeyError abcd1234 after remove_transport_action reproduces identically on clean master (stashed worktree) and with this phase diff; no existing task bead found.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: test_stranded_work_facade.py::test_reduce_stranded_work_round_trips_through_real_binding asserts schema_version 1 but the linked sase-core binding returns 2; same failure on clean master. Matches the check-run core-floor-probe that sase-core is ahead of sase-core-rs==0.43.2.

Verified sase-19m: rate-limit stderr captured before timeout yields rate_limited (ready-file sync + collect classification); timeout without that stderr stays timeout. Isolate wrapper prefers a completed worker observation over outer timeout. 20/20 serial on the flake node, 55 xdist probe tests. Unrelated scoped-lane failures reproduced on clean master or match sase-1oo/sase-1pr/sase-1on; recorded as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. No --epic-symbol leftovers.

IMPLEMENTATION: Added an evidence-based freshness preflight before `just check`, `check-full`, and standalone Symvision. It queries live bead statuses in batches and, for known closed rows, compares local Justfile rows and HEAD against a freshly fetched default-branch snapshot. Rust owns row parsing and the structured stale-checkout/local-invalid/upstream-unresolved/uncertain classification. Uncertainty refuses early without claiming upstream cleanliness. Existing close guard, closed-bead Symvision refusal, and whitelist policy remain in force. The preflight leaves worktree and index contents untouched.

REGRESSION: Added a two-clone/bare-remote/shared-bead-store reproduction. It publishes row cleanup and source-symbol cleanup, closes through the real guard, proves an old observer with live closed status is refused while retaining staged unrelated work, and proves the refusal disappears after normal cleanup integration. Added coverage for batched status lookups, open re-key owners, no-row fast path, and failed-fetch uncertainty.

VERIFICATION: Focused Python suite passed: 57 tests across epic-symbol freshness, symbol handling, close regressions, and Justfile gate ordering. Targeted core parser/classifier tests passed (5); PyO3 binding round-trip passed (1). Standalone Symvision passed (ToolRun c2ddff65c46849e5a7d348fb5a72ef2a). Primary `sase tool run check` passed (ToolRun df23e9adb95ba6cf8f3199f74030a154); linked `sase-core` `sase tool run check` passed (ToolRun 990ae82963ca4e994333f58cc86cd173). Phase has no remaining `--epic-symbol` rows. The first primary check exposed private cross-module imports in this implementation; those boundaries were corrected and the subsequent Symvision and full check passed. The published core pin was left unchanged for host completion.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-o7 — Stale observer checkouts now receive an early evidence-based refusal when live closed-bead whitelist rows remain, with a regression for the delayed-discovery path.
Implementation and regression evidence recorded in phase note #2; primary and linked core checks passed, and no phase epic-symbol rows remain.

payload.entry:
IMPLEMENTATION + MEASUREMENTS (clean base 078e3da1d6, Python 3.14.7, metric v1):
- tools/_tui_import_footprint.py (new, typed, added to typecheck_extensionless_tools) is the single probe+metric shared by tools/tui_import_closure and tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py. Footprint = UTF-8 bytes of significant tokens of the unique source files behind imported sase.* modules; ast picks excluded spans (imports, real docstrings, literal-string __all__ list/tuple assignments), tokenize measures original source. Source paths come from the modules the fresh interpreter actually imported; reading/parsing happens in the caller after counts, sys.modules and deferred results are captured, so measuring never inflates module counts or the import stopwatch.
- Cap: baseline 12,158,388 B + 4,096 allowance = 12,162,484, strict <. Kept: deferred-module list (identical), _MAX_TOTAL_MODULE_COUNT = 3904, 5.0s CPU / two-attempt policy. Module counts are diagnostics only; the old 2861 module cap is gone.
- Replays under the SAME cap (isolated git-archive snapshots in this workspace, same venv deps, removed afterwards): eef22a0124^ -> eef22a0124: 2860 -> 2863 modules, 12,160,347 -> 12,160,635 B (+288). bffbc8effd^ -> bffbc8effd: 2855 -> 2860, 12,153,966 -> 12,154,025 (+59). 362fcb2e7f^ -> 362fcb2e7f: 2856 -> 2860, 12,138,357 -> 12,138,426 (+69). d3d26a5b55 (reported failing tree): 2863 modules, 12,160,635 B, 1,849 under the cap. The deltas match the plan's prototype exactly. The OLD test run in an isolated d3d26a5b55 snapshot reproduced `assert 2863 < 2861`.
- tools/tui_import_closure now prints footprint, signed footprint change, per-source contributors (including changed contents of modules present on both sides; a net-zero split says 'footprint unchanged overall; source moved across N modules'), and keeps added/removed modules. No new CLI option.
- Tests: tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py (11), tests/test_tui_import_footprint.py (20, new), tests/test_tui_import_closure.py (11), shared real temp-package fixtures in tests/_tui_import_fixtures.py. Real fresh-subprocess proofs: facade+helpers split (repeated import/docstring boilerplate) keeps identical footprint and passes a cap with zero headroom; a new eager unrelated module trips an unchanged fixture cap; growth > 4,096 B trips the production allowance; small growth stays inside it; a previously deferred module fails independent of size and the message names it; third-party growth stays outside; strict equality fails; unicode/semicolon/alias/namespace/.pyc/missing-source/f-string brace cases covered.
- Overhead (separate from app import CPU of ~2.2s): footprint parse of the 2,860 sources is ~9s cold on a calm host (10-20s under load), 0.18s warm. A content-hash cache (in memory for tools; pytest cache dir for the real-app test, salted by helper source + interpreter) makes --diff parse only differing files and warm test runs ~7s.
- Docs: only the 'TUI import-budget ratchet' section of docs/contribute/perf-runbook.md was rewritten. No memory edits.
- Verification: just fix; sase tool run check 956013dd7868f03dca4572ee25b5562b succeeded (every stage, 583s) on the implementation. A rerun after a comment/wording-only tweak (a0017ac0a6d4fa79092b7070e0cd8c16) escalated to the full suite (core-identity-changed): 59,683 passed, 2 failed, both KNOWN and unrelated (see PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP). 45 focused tests pass.
- Limitation: the 4,096 B allowance admits small code growth by design. Real feature work is ~800 B per commit on average (tools/tui_import_closure --diff HEAD~12 shows +9,553 B across 12 commits, e.g. sase.monitor.settlement +4,464), so attributed cap raises per the test-comment policy should be expected; deferred-module exclusion stays absolute.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-1ic — the TUI import guard now enforces a strict-< normalized source-footprint cap (12,158,388 B baseline at 078e3da1d6 + 4,096 = 12,162,484) instead of a first-party module count. Replays of eef22a0124, bffbc8effd and 362fcb2e7f (+288/+59/+69 B for +3/+5/+4 modules) and d3d26a5b55 (2,863 modules, 12,160,635 B) all pass the same cap unedited; real-subprocess fixtures prove a mechanical split is neutral while a new eager source import (and a >4,096 B one) and a previously deferred module still fail; deferred list, 3904 total cap and 5.0s CPU policy unchanged; sase tool run check 956013dd... succeeded.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: tests/test_pending_actions.py::test_transport_adapter_preserves_handled_state_and_original_lifecycle (KeyError 'abcd1234') and tests/test_stranded_work_facade.py::test_reduce_stranded_work_round_trips_through_real_binding (StrandedWorkReport schema_version 2, expected 1) fail identically on the clean base 078e3da1d6 (reproduced with this phase's changes stashed) against the installed sase_core_rs 0.43.3 binding built from the ahead sase-core checkout (check run a0017ac0a6d4fa79092b7070e0cd8c16, triage KNOWN) — pending-action and stranded-work wire/binding revision drift, unrelated to the import budget.

Verified: strict-< normalized footprint cap 12,162,484 (baseline 12,158,388 + 4,096); replays of eef22a0124, bffbc8effd, 362fcb2e7f and d3d26a5b55 pass unchanged; real-subprocess fixtures prove split neutrality, eager-import and deferred-module failures; deferred list, total cap and CPU policy unchanged; just fix + sase tool run check 956013dd... succeeded (rerun's only failures were two KNOWN clean-base failures recorded as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP).

LANDED at sase master 31a28d9618 with sase-core pin e60f3e1658 (sase-core master tip). VERIFIED: all 5 phases are closed, and each TASK RESOLVED claim was checked against source and commits.
(.1) sase 5585fadefd + core e60f3e16: epic-symbol freshness preflight runs before check, check-full, and _lint-symvision. The close guard and symvision policy are unchanged.
(.2) sase 5d7a79c3c0: the import budget is now a strict normalized source-footprint cap (12,162,484 B). The deferred list, total-module bound, and CPU policy are kept.
(.3) core 02eb6961: the FederationLock guard explicitly unlocks on Drop.
(.4) sase 0760eb0100: the PTY helper always prepends a test-owned sase.
(.5) sase 34a8638ee0: the AGY probe drains pipes before and after the kill, and the isolate wrapper keeps completed observations.
The DECISION keep_five_seeds was honored: no feature or memory edits beyond the five seeds. Seed tasks sase-o7, sase-1ic, sase-1gz, sase-13a, and sase-19m were closed done with evidence. Lander runs on HEAD after reinstalling the venv against core e60f3e16: 158 focused tests across all five areas pass under -n 4; test_app_import_budget 11/11; the freshness preflight exits 0 in 0.3s.
INTEGRATION: post-start commits c56f4201a6 (test split), c5fdcd10cd, a5bc2987cc (docs), and 31a28d9618 neither conflict with nor duplicate the epic. No Python --epic-symbol parser remains outside the Rust binding. 31a28d9618 grew the TUI footprint by 1,378 B in existing modules and stays under the cap with 1,326 B headroom, which is the intended attributed-raise ratchet.
FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE:
(a) test_pending_actions KeyError abcd1234 (sase-1qn.2 #4, sase-1qn.5 #3): declined, already fixed on master by c5fdcd10cd (sase-1qk.6) and passing at HEAD.
(b) test_stranded_work_facade schema_version 2 vs 1 (sase-1qn.2 #4, sase-1qn.5 #4): declined, fixed by 31a28d9618 (asserts 2; core 154fe9e2 is in the pin) and passing at HEAD.
(c) Scoped-lane nodes from ToolRun 4062c1f3 (sase-1qn.5 #2): corroborated through /sase_new_task with +1 on sase-1oo (claim-check holders and tombstone; sase-1op is already merged there), sase-1pr, and sase-1on. The same run's unproposed oracle and loader nodes pass 54/54 under -n 4 at HEAD, so no task was filed.
No --epic-symbol entries remained.

BACKLOG CHAIN (sase-1qn.land, 2026-11-01, sase 31a28d9618): re-listed 387 non-closed tasks. No duplicate or obsolete closures: sase-zo still reproduces through 'sase repo list -p sase' (exit 2, no WORKSPACE_DIR); sase-1q3 still gives 7 failed with SASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE=sonnet; sase-lk is dormant. Recurring full-run master-red nodes (contract manifest, monitor start ack and supervisor, completion snapshot, capacity scans, audits) pass 110/110 at HEAD. New finding: the prompt-render cluster sase-1ia, sase-1l3, and sase-1hy reproduces on apollo at 31a28d9618 (7-9 failed of 30) and passes 30/30 on athena. Ruled out: Python 3.12 vs 3.14, the core binding, HOME/XDG config, env -i, the git-archive layout, and TZ=UTC. Proposed next epic sase_plan_task_backlog_epic_5.md: apollo prompt-render (sase-1ia, sase-1l3, sase-1hy), agents-sync drain flake (sase-xo), sase-core sudo_runner ETXTBSY (sase-15h). Next in line: sase-1q3, sase-zo, sase-1em, sase-1oy.
